annotations.description: A detector raised {{ $labels.type }}. The run was not stopped: detectors observe and alert, they never cancel a run or cap spend. Open the session dashboard and paste the session id from the trace to see the step it landed on.

_notes.why_increase_and_not_the_raw_counter: spanlight_detections_total only ever rises, so a rule on its value fires forever after the first detection and gets muted within a day. increase() over the evaluation window asks the question actually worth asking, which is whether anything fired recently.
_notes.why_the_name_is_a_regex: Prometheus appends _total to a monotonic sum when translating from OTLP, and whether it skips a name already ending in _total has varied by version. Matching both spellings costs nothing. A rule that silently matches no series is a rule that never fires, which is the failure this whole project is about.
_notes.why_for_is_zero: A detection is a discrete event, not a level to be sustained. Requiring it to persist would mean a single silent failure never alerts, which is the exact failure this project exists to surface.
_notes.why_group_by_type_and_service: The two labels the counter carries. Session id is deliberately not among them: as a metric label it would create one time series per run and exhaust the free tier's active-series limit in days, so the alert says what fired and the trace says which run.
_notes.sampling: Detections inside sampled-out sessions are not counted, because a dropped span cannot carry the attribute or the event either. At the default sample_rate of 1.0 this rule sees everything; below it, it sees the same fraction as the traces.
_notes.nodata_is_ok: A counter that has never incremented reports no series at all. Treating that as alerting would page on a healthy service that has simply never failed.
